title: Certified reduced-basis emulation of conformal field theories on the fuzzy sphere
abstract: Fuzzy-sphere regularization gives numerical access to three-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs), but locating one requires testing for criticality across the parameter space of microscopic couplings. We reduce the search cost by about two orders of magnitude, combining an exact diagonalization based on states having definite total angular momentum with a certified reduced-basis emulator that reconstructs energies, observables and their derivatives continuously across the couplings from a handful of exact solutions per system size. The combination reproduces the published ground-state-energy analysis of the fuzzy-sphere Ising model and the published conformal data of a three-flavor fuzzy-sphere realization of the O(2) Wilson--Fisher CFT, including quantities defined by parameter derivatives. Applied to the O(2) model with no CFT input, the ground-state-energy criterion locates the critical coupling to within half a percent of a density matrix renormalization group value obtained on systems more than twice the size, and maps the critical line of the model across the coupling plane. Ground-state criteria locate the critical line robustly, but the point they select along it is weakly determined, and the computed dimensions come closest to the bootstrap elsewhere along the line.
summary: This work develops a highly efficient computational framework using reduced-basis emulation combined with exact diagonalization to study CFTs on the fuzzy sphere. By accurately mapping the energy landscape across coupling parameters, the authors precisely locate critical points for the Ising and O(2) models. This methodology significantly reduces the search cost for understanding quantum critical phenomena in strongly interacting systems.
main_problem: To gain numerical access to three-dimensional Conformal Field Theories (CFTs) by efficiently testing for criticality across the vast parameter space of microscopic couplings.
main_result: The combination of exact diagonalization and a certified reduced-basis emulator successfully reproduces known CFT results for the Ising and O(2) models, locating critical lines with high precision.
method: The authors combine exact diagonalization on symmetry-adapted bases with a certified reduced-basis emulator (RBM) to reconstruct energy and observable data continuously across coupling variations, drastically reducing computational cost.
model_or_system: The study focuses on fuzzy-sphere regularizations of 3D CFTs, specifically analyzing the $N_f=2$ Ising model and the $N_f=3$ O(2) Wilson-Fisher CFT. These models are realized via Hamiltonians involving interacting fermions in the Lowest Landau Level.
key_observables: Ground-state energy ($E_{GS}$), scaling dimensions ($\Delta O$), and the ratio $\chi = E_{3/2}/E_0$ used to locate critical points.
important_parameters: Microscopic couplings (e.g., $h$ for Ising, $D$ and $V_0$ for O(2)), and system size $N$.
main_assumptions: The fuzzy-sphere construction preserves SO(3) symmetry, and the RBM assumes the Hamiltonians are exactly affine in the couplings.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the critical lines for the Ising and O(2) models in coupling planes, showing agreement between emulator results and established DMRG values. Other figures show error analysis and energy/order-parameter surfaces.
paper_structure: The paper develops the computational framework by first detailing the exact-L ED approach, then introducing the RBM for efficient parameter scanning, and finally applying this combined method to determine and map the critical lines for both the Ising and O(2) models using multiple diagnostic criteria.
why_interesting: The use of RBM to map out critical lines in parameter space is a powerful computational technique applicable to any quantum system whose Hamiltonian depends smoothly on multiple parameters, bridging the gap between exact diagonalization and full phase diagram mapping.
